newsletter.markdown:
1. **Discovery & Translational Science**

* **[Big Pharma]** **Daraxonrasib resistance mechanisms identified in pancreatic cancer** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04537-w)
  * Circulating tumor DNA analysis of 44 pancreatic cancer patients treated with the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor daraxonrasib in a Phase 1/2 trial revealed acquired genetic mechanisms driving monotherapy resistance.
  * Preclinical modeling confirmed specific bypass pathways, offering actionable targets for rational combination strategies to restore sensitivity.

* **Long-term Aβ42 active immunization reduces plaque-associated pathology for up to 14 years** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.10.26359862)
  * Post-mortem brain tissue analysis from Alzheimer's disease patients in the AN1792 trial demonstrated that active Aβ42 vaccination attenuated plaque-associated synapse loss and reduced phosphorylated-tau (AT8 and pTau217) accumulation around remaining plaques for up to 14 years post-treatment.

* **Novel 2-methoxyestradiol derivative ABRL8301 mitigates progressive pulmonary fibrosis** [PubMed](https://pubmed.org/42580509/)
  * ABRL8301, a derivative of 2-methoxyestradiol, downregulates 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase 1 (11β-HSD1) to attenuate progressive pulmonary fibrosis in preclinical models.

* **Plasma proteomic signature stratifies risk in IPMN pancreatic precursor lesions** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.09.26360008)
  * An O-link panel measuring 1,104 plasma proteins identified a cytoskeletal and extracellular matrix remodeling signature that distinguishes low-grade from high-grade dysplasia and invasive carcinoma in intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMN), complementing CA19-9 testing.

* **Immune Health Index predicts outcomes and immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.08.26360002)
  * A Multi-stage Precision Stratification framework integrating immune surveillance, exhaustion, and reserve scores (IHI) was validated across four cohorts (n = 931) as an independent prognostic factor (HR = 0.818) and predictor of clinical benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy following liver resection.

* **IL-27 receptor signaling drives cardiac remodeling in heart failure** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.05.743140)
  * Genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of the IL-27 receptor significantly suppressed transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac inflammation, fibrosis, hypertrophy, and mortality in mouse models.

* **DHODH inhibitors display broad antiviral activity against henipaviruses and arenaviruses** [PubMed](https://pubmed.org/42580486/)
  * Dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) inhibitors demonstrated potent *in vitro* antiviral efficacy against high-consequence henipaviruses and arenaviruses.

2. **Early Trials — Phase I–II**

* **[Biotech]** **Infinimmune secures $75M Series A for atopic dermatitis antibodies** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/infinimmune-atopic-dermatitis-series-a-financing-dupixent/827504/)
  * Infinimmune raised $75 million in Series A venture funding to advance its first two antibody candidates into clinical development for atopic dermatitis.
  * The programs aim to target novel mechanisms to overcome current biologic limitations, including slow onset and incomplete patient response rates seen with Dupixent.

* **[Biotech]** **Epicrispr Biotechnologies raises $90M Series C for epigenetic editor in FSHD** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/epicrispr-series-c-epigenetic-editing-fshd/827340/)
  * Epicrispr completed enrollment in an early-stage study evaluating EPI-321, a CRISPR-based epigenetic editing therapy designed to silence DUX4 expression without breaking DNA in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD).
  * The $90 million funding will support clinical advancement of EPI-321 and the broader epigenetic editing platform.

* **[Biotech]** **Skylark Bio launches gene therapy trial for genetic deafness** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/11/skylark-bio-gjb2-otoferlin-gene-therapies-for-deafness/)
  * Skylark Bio initiated a clinical study evaluating gene therapies targeting GJB2 and otoferlin genetic mutations responsible for congenital hearing loss.

* **[Biotech]** **Incyte evaluates three oral PD-L1 inhibitors in Phase 1 trial** [PubMed](https://pubmed.org/42580817/)
  * A Phase 1 dose-evaluation study established safety, pharmacodynamics, and target biomarker responses for three oral small-molecule PD-L1 inhibitors: INCB086550, INCB099280, and INCB099318.

3. **Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III**

* **[Biotech]** **Vaderis Therapeutics closes $152M Series B and begins Phase 3 HHT trial** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/vaderis-series-b-engasertib-hht-akt-inhibitor/827466/)
  * Vaderis initiated a pivotal trial testing its oral AKT inhibitor, engasertib, for the treatment of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT), a rare genetic vascular disease.
  * The $152 million capital raise provides funding through potential commercialization projected by 2029.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Semaglutide 2.4 mg demonstrates health utility gains in MASH** [PubMed](https://pubmed.org/42580587/)
  * An EQ-5D health utility analysis of the Phase 3 ESSENCE trial revealed significant quality-of-life improvements in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and stage F2/F3 fibrosis treated with once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg.

* **Statin discontinuation in low-risk adults over 75 does not increase mortality** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/11/stop-statins-age-75-lancet-study-suggests-safe-healthy-adults/)
  * A study published in *The Lancet* showed that stopping statins in primary-prevention individuals aged 75 and older with low cardiovascular risk did not result in increased overall or cardiovascular mortality.

4. **Regulatory & Approvals**

* **[Biotech]** **Rhythm Pharmaceuticals gains UK expanded authorization for Imcivree** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2087147468328727011)
  * The UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) expanded marketing authorization for Imcivree (setmelanotide) to include chronic weight management and hunger control in patients with acquired hypothalamic obesity resulting from hypothalamic injury.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Fresenius Kabi recalls Tyenne lot due to glass particulate contamination** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/fresenius-kabi-issues-nationwide-recall-tyenner-tocilizumab-aazg-injection-400-mg20-ml-vials-due)
  * Fresenius Kabi issued a voluntary user-level recall for one lot of Tyenne (tocilizumab-aazg) injection (400 mg/20 mL) after internal testing detected glass particles in vials.

* **FDA rejects radiopharmaceutical candidate over manufacturing deficiencies** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/08/11/fda-rejects-radiopharmaceutical-340b-court-battles/)
  * The FDA issued a Complete Response Letter rejecting an undisclosed radiopharmaceutical therapy candidate due to manufacturing quality control issues, delaying a potential competitor in the market.

5. **Business & Strategy**

* **[Biotech]** **Mereo BioPharma licenses alvelestat option to Sentynl Therapeutics** [X / Twitter](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2087149062784946466)
  * Mereo BioPharma executed an option and license agreement with Sentynl Therapeutics for alvelestat in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency-associated lung disease.
  * Mereo receives an upfront option fee and is eligible for $40 million upon option exercise, alongside up to $435 million in prospective milestone payments.

* **[Biotech]** **K2 Therapeutics launches with $50M seed round led by Ying Huang** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/k2-ying-huang-biotech-startup-mpm-china-drugs/827544/)
  * Startup K2 Therapeutics launched with $50 million in seed financing from MPM BioImpact and appointed former Legend Biotech CEO Ying Huang as chief executive.
  * K2 holds eight preclinical and clinical-stage assets, including an early-stage antibody-drug conjugate and a dual T-cell engager in-licensed from China-based Adcoris and Antengene.

* **[Biotech]** **MoonLake Immunotherapeutics faces scrutiny over clinical data transparency** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/11/why-is-moonlake-immunotherapeutics-scared-of-releasing-data/)
  * Industry analysts raised questions regarding MoonLake's reluctance to disclose granular dataset details for its lead clinical candidate.

6. **Public Health & Policy**

* **Executive order proposes major changes to US childhood immunization schedule** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/trump-executive-order-childhood-vaccine-schedule-autism/827510/)
  * President Trump signed the "Gold Standard Childhood Vaccine Recommendations" executive order seeking to lower universally recommended childhood vaccines from 17 to 11, break the combined MMR vaccine into three separate shots, and require single-vaccine appointments.
  * Medical organizations, epidemiologists, and biopharma stakeholders pushed back, pointing to a lack of scientific justification and warning that unbundling vaccines risks lower compliance and increased exposure to preventable childhood diseases [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/11/how-we-know-splitting-up-mmr-vaccine-could-be-dangerous/), [Science](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/proposed-changes-childhood-vaccination-strongly-felt-opinion).

* **Administration plans Medicaid funding cut for pediatric gender-affirming care** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/11/medicaid-to-end-funding-gender-affirming-care-transgender-youth/)
  * The White House outlined plans to restrict federal Medicaid reimbursement for specific gender-affirming interventions in transgender minors.

* **Medicare GLP-1 program framework risks limiting patient uptake** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/11/medicare-weight-loss-drugs-glp-1s-bridge-program-primary-care/)
  * Primary care clinicians warned that administrative complexities built into Medicare's new bridge program for $50/month GLP-1 weight loss drugs may create barriers to access.

**Worth watching:** Biopharma industry and physician pushback against executive orders restructuring vaccine administration schedules, which could affect commercial vaccine manufacturing schedules and pediatric delivery logistics.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [BPC-157: great marketing, not great science](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/oHl8saf_rPA) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Evaluates the scientific evidence and safety considerations surrounding BPC-157, a widely promoted healing peptide.
        - Examines the effects of CJC-1295 on growth hormone levels and whether it translates to improvements in strength, recovery, or body composition.
        - Discusses the relationship between gray market peptides and the pharmaceutical drug pipeline.
        - Outlines genuine near-term therapeutic applications for peptides in metabolism, cancer, infectious diseases, and diagnostics.
    - [Why ChatGPT Can’t Replace Doctors](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/BJFRqLyJSog) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Features George Mathew discussing the major obstacles preventing AI solutions like ChatGPT from replacing doctors in healthcare.
        - Highlights medical licensing and legal liability as primary structural barriers to healthcare AI adoption.
        - Outlines the key limitations and ethical challenges facing medical AI implementations.
    - [Why do so many healthcare AI projects succeed in pilot programs but never reach production?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2FFKn4iEzmg) -- Health2Tech
        - Explains that model accuracy and performance are rarely the primary reasons healthcare AI pilots fail to reach enterprise production.
        - Details how healthcare organizations evaluate security, data governance, explainability, vendor risk, and system architecture prior to deployment.
        - Emphasizes the necessity of designing healthcare AI architectures for trust, regulatory compliance, and security from day one to avoid enterprise delays.
- Pure Science
    - [How long is a day on the sun?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/bU9xvXyWrdk) -- minutephysics
        - Explains that because the sun is composed of flowing plasma, its rotation period relative to distant stars varies by latitude: roughly 24.5 Earth days at the equator and 34 Earth days near the poles.
        - Notes that if defined strictly by time duration, a day on the sun is slightly longer than an Earth day due to gravitational time dilation.
        - Clarifies that defining a day based on the sun returning overhead is geometrically inapplicable directly on the sun itself.
- Other
    - [How did ocean invertebrates end up on Mt. Everest?!](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/2Gc77M1OZwc) -- CrashCourse
        - Raises the geological question of how fossils of ocean-dwelling invertebrates were deposited at the elevation of Mt. Everest.
        - Links the presence of marine fossils on high mountain summits to geological tectonic processes like orogeny.
        - Outlines community funding and support mechanisms for Crash Course's educational video content.
